summary: This informational document defines TLS cipher suites that use the ARIA block cipher, a Korean encryption standard. Adding them lets TLS connections use ARIA for encrypting data. It is not on the standards track.

eli5.summary: TLS lets two computers talk secretly, and they must agree on a secret code method. This document adds one more method, called ARIA, to the menu.

questions: what is aria cipher in tls
which tls cipher suites use aria
subtitle: Registers 54 TLS cipher suites that use the Korean ARIA block cipher, with SHA-2 hashes, GCM and pre-shared keys.

tldr.problem: TLS had no cipher suites for ARIA, a block cipher that is a Korean standard and has been widely used in Korea.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines cipher suites that pair ARIA with the key exchanges of TLS 1.2, using either CBC mode with a SHA-2 HMAC or Galois Counter Mode (GCM), plus pre-shared key variants.
tldr.outcome: IANA allocated the code points 0xC0,0x3C through 0xC0,0x71 in the TLS Cipher Suite Registry. The RFC is Informational and has since been updated by RFC 10015.

today: RFC 6209 is an Informational RFC, not a standards track document, and it has been updated by RFC 10015. It was not obsoleted.

sections.title: Why ARIA Needs Cipher Suites
sections.content:
This document specifies cipher suites for Transport Layer Security (TLS) so that the ARIA encryption algorithm can be used as a block cipher. It builds on RFC 5246 (TLS 1.2) and on the ARIA description in RFC 5794.

The suites use the SHA-2 family of hash functions and ARIA in Galois Counter Mode. Elliptic curve suites and pre-shared key (PSK) suites are also defined. Suites with SHA-1 are left out on purpose, because recent analytic work on SHA-1 led the IETF to move gradually toward stronger hash algorithms.
sections.eli5: A cipher suite is a recipe card for how two computers will scramble their messages. This document writes new recipe cards that use the ARIA scrambler.

sections.title: The ARIA Cipher
sections.content:
ARIA is a general-purpose block cipher developed by Korean cryptographers in 2003. It is an iterated block cipher with 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys, and it encrypts 128-bit blocks in 12, 14 or 16 rounds, depending on the key size.

The RFC says it became a Korean standard block cipher algorithm in 2004 and has been widely used in Korea, especially for government-to-public services. It was included in PKCS #11 in 2007. The algorithm itself and its object identifiers are described in RFC 5794, not here.
sections.eli5: ARIA is a scrambling method invented in Korea. It chops a message into pieces and scrambles each piece several rounds in a row.

sections.title: The Defined Cipher Suites
sections.content:
The suites come in three groups, each with 128-bit and 256-bit key variants. The first twenty use ARIA in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with a SHA-2 family HMAC; eight of those twenty use elliptic curves. The next twenty use the same asymmetric algorithms but with ARIA in Galois Counter Mode (GCM), the authenticated encryption mode defined for TLS 1.2.

The last fourteen are PSK suites: eight use an HMAC and six use ARIA GCM. Names follow the pattern TLS_RSA_WITH_ARIA_128_CBC_SHA256, where the key exchange comes first, then the cipher and key size, then the hash. The 128-bit suites end in SHA256 and the 256-bit CBC suites in SHA384.
sections.eli5: There are three boxes of recipe cards: one with a chained scrambler, one with a scrambler that also checks nobody tampered, and one for computers that already share a secret.

sections.title: How the Suites Work
sections.content:
The RSA, DHE_RSA, DH_RSA, DHE_DSS, DH_DSS, DH_anon, ECDH and ECDHE key exchanges are performed as defined in RFC 5246. The ARIA_128_CBC suites use a 128-bit key and a 128-bit initialization vector (IV); the ARIA_256_CBC suites use a 256-bit key and a 128-bit IV.

The GCM suites are defined by analogy with AES GCM (RFC 5116, RFC 5288), because AES and ARIA share key sizes and block length. The pseudorandom function (PRF) SHALL be the TLS PRF using SHA-256 for suites ending in _SHA256, and SHA-384 for suites ending in _SHA384. PSK suites are described in RFC 4279, RFC 4785, RFC 5487 and RFC 5489.
sections.eli5: The new recipes reuse the old handshake steps and only swap in the ARIA scrambler. Which strength of checking is used depends on the name at the end of the recipe.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that at the time of writing no security problems had been found on ARIA, and cites a paper on integral attacks against reduced-round ARIA. It adds that the security considerations of RFC 4279, RFC 4785, RFC 5116, RFC 5288, RFC 5289, RFC 5487 and the NIST GCM specification apply to this document as well.
sections.eli5: When this was written, nobody had found a way to break ARIA. The older safety rules for similar recipes still apply.

sections.title: IANA Allocations
sections.content: IANA has allocated the suites in the TLS Cipher Suite Registry. The values run from { 0xC0,0x3C } (TLS_RSA_WITH_ARIA_128_CBC_SHA256) to { 0xC0,0x71 } (TLS_ECDHE_PSK_WITH_ARIA_256_CBC_SHA384), in the same order as they are listed in the document.
sections.eli5: Each recipe card got its own number in the official list so every computer knows which card is meant.
